page_title: The IDE for agentic engineering – Fletch

sources.entry: Fletch - Native IDE for AI coding agents, giving each agent a sandboxed clone of your repository plus a shared symbol and call-graph index, with diff review before merge. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/fwdai/fletch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Fletch
summary.one_liner: Fletch is a native macOS IDE for running multiple AI coding agents in parallel, each in its own sandboxed clone of a repository, chained into review-gated workflows.
use_cases: Running several coding agents on different tasks at once
Planning, building, reviewing and testing a feature with specialist agents
Reviewing agent-written diffs before committing or merging
Orchestrating Claude, Codex or Cursor CLIs under one pipeline
Keeping agent changes isolated from your main repository
summary.what_it_does: Fletch runs coding agents in parallel, giving each agent its own full clone of the repository under a write sandbox or Docker container. Users can define workflows that chain specialist agents (architect, coder, reviewer, tester) with a gate at each step, such as plan approval, review clean, or tests passing. It drives existing CLIs like claude, codex, cursor-agent and opencode, and integrates reviewers such as Greptile and CI or test commands. The interface shows live diffs, lets the user review changes, and supports committing, opening and merging a PR from the app.
notable: Each agent gets a full cloned repo in a hard sandbox rather than a shared git worktree
Workflows chain architect, coder, reviewer and tester agents with gates at every step
Uses the official CLIs and subscriptions you already have, with no middleman API keys
Local-first: source stays in your git and Fletch servers do not see code
caveats: Windows and Linux are listed as roadmap items, not available
Relies on external agent CLIs and subscriptions the user already pays for
